title: A new chapter for June: our founding team is joining Amplitude
html:
After five incredible years of building new ways of understanding how people use products, we have an important update to share: June will officially wind down operations.

The founding team will be joining Amplitude to continue pushing forward a vision we still deeply believe in: help companies build better digital products and experiences.

As part of this transition, the June standalone product will wind down on August 8, 2025.

What this means for you

If you're a customer, here’s what happens next:

  • You have 30 days to export your data or migrate to Amplitude. ​We’ve put together an export tool to download your data and a migration guide to move your data into Amplitude.
    ​
  • Final invoice & refunds:
    • If you're on a monthly subscription, you’ll only be charged for the days between your last renewal date and August 8, 2025. Since we bill at the end of each period, your final charge will be prorated to reflect just those days. You’ll continue to have full access to your current plan (Growth or Pro) until August 8 to complete your export or migration.
    • If you’re on a yearly or multi-year subscription, we’ll refund you the unused days of your contract, specifically, the days between August 9, 2025, and your original contract end date. Refunds will be processed starting next week.
      ​
      In all cases, you’ll retain full access to the product and our support during the next 30 days to ensure a smooth transition.

We’ll remain fully available until the last day. Whether via email, Intercom, or your private Slack or WhatsApp channels. Nothing changes there. We’ll help you every step of the way.

A thank you

It’s hard to explain what these four years meant to us.

We woke up every single day thinking about you, our customers. What you needed. What we should build next. How to make onboarding smoother. Which bugs to fix. How to tell our story. How to win your trust.

For over five years, June has been our obsession. It shaped how we lived, what we talked about, the people we met, the way we thought. It’s not just been work, it’s been the most valuable and intense learning experience of our lives.

Thank you for being part of this journey. Whether you were an early believer who signed up when we were barely more than a dashboard or someone who just discovered us last month, you’ve been the reason we kept going. Your feedback, your ideas, your encouragement, your honesty. It all mattered more than you know.

You helped us carve out a space in a crowded market, one where we were never supposed to win. And yet, somehow, we did. We grew. We reached profitability (not every month, but close). We built something small and strong that we’re proud of.

And of course, a special thanks to the June team. Past and present (Vinayak, Daniel, Pranav, Alberto, Adis, Eugenio). They're the most amazing people we've had the chance to work with 🙌

Why we’re making this choice

From day one, we believed you didn’t need a massive team to build something great. We built June with a small, focused crew because we believed that clarity, speed, and obsession would outweigh the need for a large headcount. And in many ways, we still believe that.

But our space is tough. It’s crowded. It’s complex. It demands precision, scalability, and deep integrations across an entire stack. Building a product analytics tool for companies of all sizes that is simple and accessible, is extremely hard. And so, recently, we asked ourselves: where can we, as individuals, have the most impact?

The honest answer brought us here. If you know Amplitude, you know they’ve been pioneers in the product analytics space for over a decade. They’ve built an incredible platform that helps some of the world’s most innovative companies understand their users, build better product experiences, and drive growth. Amplitude has always gone deeper than anyone else: serious infrastructure, deep insights. And now they’re building on top of it, turning analytics into a more complete product toolkit for teams that want to go from insight to action without switching tools

When we first started talking with Spenser and the Amplitude team, we quickly realized we could have a bigger impact together. We share the same core belief: analytics should empower, not overwhelm. By joining Amplitude, we'll have the scale to deliver more value, serve more teams, and help build the future of the digital analytics category. You'll get to see that impact if you decide to follow us there.

We’ll be writing more soon. Posts to reflect on this adventure, share the highs and lows, and open up about the lessons we’ve learned along the way.

But for now, just know this: we’re grateful beyond words. And we’re hopeful for what comes next. We’ll be here, fully present, until the very last day.

After that, you’ll find us at Amplitude. Still building. Still listening.

With love 💜
Enzo, Ferruccio

title: CRM vs. CSP: Choosing the Right Tool for Customer Growth in B2B SaaS
html:
If you work in customer success or sales at a B2B SaaS company, you’ve probably heard the same question more than once: should we use a CRM or a Customer Success Platform (CSP) to manage customer relationships?

At first glance, it’s easy to assume one might replace the other. But in reality, each tool solves a different part of the customer journey.

When your goal is growth through stronger retention, deeper engagement, and more predictable expansion, it’s worth getting clear on what each platform does—and what your business actually needs. For many companies, especially in the earlier stages of growth, the right answer isn’t one or the other. It’s knowing how to use them together and when to layer in extra capability.

What CRMs Do Well

Customer Relationship Management systems—HubSpot, Salesforce, Attio and the like—were built to help sales and marketing teams organize prospects, track conversations, and manage pipelines. Their job is to guide leads through the buying journey until a deal is closed.

In that sense, CRMs act as the system of record for everything pre-sale. They centralize contacts, communication history, company information, and deal stages. For teams focused on growth, this level of visibility and coordination is essential.

But CRMs weren’t originally designed with post-sale engagement in mind.

Once the deal closes, the customer record often goes quiet. You might log some account activity or renewal dates, but the platform itself doesn’t offer much insight into what’s actually happening inside the product. This becomes a problem when your revenue depends on renewals, upsells, and adoption. If you can’t see whether a customer is truly succeeding, how can you help them grow?

Where Customer Success Platforms Excel

Customer Success Platforms, or CSPs, were created to solve this exact blind spot. Tools like Gainsight, Catalyst, and Totango are built to monitor ongoing customer engagement. They help CS teams track onboarding progress, log health scores, surface churn risks, and automate key touchpoints like QBRs or renewal reminders.

CSPs give post-sale teams a structured way to operate, offering powerful segmentation and workflow automation tailored to the customer journey. They bring product usage data into view, helping teams act on it with greater clarity and speed.

But CSPs come with their own set of challenges. They’re often expensive, require dedicated ownership, and come with a learning curve. For smaller teams or early-stage SaaS businesses, implementing a CSP can feel like overkill—especially when the same outcome could be achieved by enhancing the tools they already use.

When a CRM Is Enough

If your company is in the $1M to $5M ARR range, and your customer success motion is still taking shape, your CRM might be all you need. It’s already connected to your customer records, sales pipeline, and email history. Your team knows how to use it. It’s familiar and flexible.

The key to making a CRM work for CS is configuration. With the right custom properties, lifecycle stages, and pipelines, you can track onboarding status, renewal likelihood, feature adoption, and engagement level—all within the same system. You can even set up alerts and task queues to prompt follow-ups and interventions.

Of course, the CRM alone won’t show you how customers are using your product. That’s where things get interesting.

Adding Product Usage Data to the CRM

The turning point for most teams comes when they connect product data to the CRM. Suddenly, what was once just a sales tool becomes a full-view customer intelligence platform.

June was designed specifically to make this connection seamless. It integrates with your product to track how users are engaging—what features they’re using, how often they log in, whether they’re stuck or thriving. Then it pushes that data into your CRM, enriching each customer record with insights that matter for success, not just sales.

This integration changes the game. Your customer success team no longer has to guess who’s at risk or who’s ready to expand. They can see it, act on it, and track the results—all from inside their CRM.

When to Add a CSP

There does come a time when a dedicated CSP starts to make sense. If your company is approaching $10M+ ARR, has a team of CSMs managing hundreds of accounts, or needs complex segmentation and orchestration, then a CSP can add structure and efficiency.

At this level, you’re likely managing multiple customer tiers with different engagement models—tech-touch, low-touch, high-touch. A CSP gives you the tools to standardize success plans, run health scoring at scale, and align renewal playbooks across the team.

Still, even with a CSP in place, the CRM doesn’t go away. You’ll always need a source of truth for contacts, deals, and revenue data. That’s why the most successful SaaS teams don’t think in terms of CRM vs. CSP—they think in terms of integration.

How June Fits In

June helps companies make their existing stack smarter. If you’re running your customer success motion out of HubSpot or Salesforce, June acts as the missing link between what your customers do and what your team sees.

It lets you build dashboards that track feature usage, set up alerts when engagement drops, and identify the customers who are ready for a check-in, a renewal conversation, or an upsell.

Because June connects product data with CRM data, it supports both sales and customer success use cases. You get a unified view of the customer—from acquisition to expansion—with no need to introduce another tool just to get started.

For many B2B SaaS companies, especially those in verticals with specialized workflows and non-technical users, this kind of visibility is critical. You don’t just want to know who your customer is—you want to know what they’re doing and how to help them succeed.

Choosing the Right Tool for the Right Stage

The decision between a CRM and a CSP isn’t about picking sides. It’s about understanding where your company is, how your teams work, and what data you need to serve your customers better.

If you're early in your growth journey and your CS team is small or just forming, the CRM is a solid foundation—especially if you enhance it with product data through a tool like June. If you’re further along and need deeper orchestration, a CSP may be worth the investment. And if you’re looking to future-proof your tech stack, it’s worth thinking about how all your tools work together—not just what each does on its own.

June makes that integration simple, actionable, and scalable.

Because when you’re growing a SaaS business, success isn’t just about closing deals—it’s about making sure your customers stick around.

title: Turning HubSpot Into a Customer Success Powerhouse: A Practical Guide for B2B SaaS
html:
For many teams, HubSpot is synonymous with inbound marketing.

But over time, HubSpot has quietly become much more than a place to track MQLs and manage email workflows. With its evolution into a full-fledged CRM platform, it now holds real potential for supporting an entirely different side of the business: customer success.

In the world of B2B SaaS—especially for companies with smaller CS teams or hybrid roles—the line between sales, onboarding, and customer success is often blurry. And while many CS teams still rely on spreadsheets, internal notes, or disconnected tools, there’s a growing recognition that a structured CRM, like HubSpot, can provide a much-needed system of record for managing customer relationships beyond the deal close.

HubSpot is not out-of-the-box built for CS. But with the right configuration, it can become a surprisingly powerful hub for managing renewals, driving adoption, and improving retention.

TL;DR

  • HubSpot can be transformed into a powerful customer success tool when tailored with custom workflows, properties, and lifecycle stages designed for post-sale engagement.
  • The real value emerges when product usage data is integrated directly into HubSpot, giving CS teams full visibility into adoption, behavior, and health signals.
  • June connects your product analytics with HubSpot, enabling automated, real-time insights that drive proactive retention and expansion strategies.
  • For lean B2B SaaS teams, this setup creates a scalable and cost-effective CS engine using the tools they already rely on—no need for a separate, complex platform.

Building a Customer Success Workflow in HubSpot

One of the most immediate benefits of using HubSpot for customer success is the shared visibility. Since most companies already have sales, marketing, and onboarding in HubSpot, you avoid yet another disconnected tool. Instead, you get continuity across the customer journey—if you know how to set it up.

To do this well, you need to tailor the object structure and lifecycle stages to include post-sale activities. Custom properties can be added to track things like onboarding milestones, product usage health, time-to-value, or renewal likelihood. Custom pipelines can be created for renewals or expansion. And playbooks can guide your team through consistent CS touchpoints based on account maturity or engagement status.

What makes this possible is HubSpot’s flexibility. While it won’t behave like a traditional customer success platform out of the box, it gives you the tools to build your own process—and adapt it as your company grows.

Why Product Data Integration Changes the Game

Here’s the part where things get really interesting. Managing customer success from HubSpot is useful—but it becomes exponentially more powerful when you combine it with product data. Because even the most detailed renewal playbook won’t help you if you don’t know whether your customer is actually using the product.

That’s where integrating HubSpot with June comes in.

June connects product usage data to your CRM, enriching every account and contact in HubSpot with insights like activation progress, feature adoption, usage frequency, and health scores. This allows your CS team to see product engagement alongside lifecycle stage, contract value, or last touchpoint—without having to jump between platforms.

It also unlocks automation that actually makes sense. For example, you can trigger a Slack alert when a high-value customer hasn't logged in for 10 days. Or create a follow-up task in HubSpot when a customer crosses a usage milestone. Or segment your entire book of business based on a combination of behavior and commercial value. It’s where customer success becomes genuinely proactive.

Making HubSpot Work for Retention and Expansion

Customer success is not only about preventing churn. It's also about uncovering opportunities—upsells, cross-sells, deeper adoption. And for many B2B SaaS companies, the moment a customer expands their usage or buys another seat is more valuable than the initial deal.

With June + HubSpot, those signals become visible.

Let’s say a customer adds a new team or starts using a secondary feature set. That behavior can be tracked automatically and surfaced inside your CRM. Your team doesn’t have to guess who to contact about expansion—they see the evidence and act. That’s how product-led growth and sales-led expansion can finally work together: same source of truth, same workflow, shared data.

Even customer marketing can benefit. HubSpot workflows can now be enriched with behavioral data. Want to send a tailored webinar invite only to users who engaged heavily with a new feature? That’s no longer a guess—it’s a workflow step.

A Use Case That’s Closer Than You Think

You don’t need to be a massive company to benefit from this setup.

In fact, if you’re in that $1–10M ARR stage with a lean CS team, this approach may be even more valuable. You likely don’t have the resources to roll out a dedicated CS platform and train a team on it. But you already have HubSpot. With June, you can plug in your product data, start tracking what matters, and build workflows that actually reflect what your customers are doing.

A few hours of setup can give you a retention engine that supports onboarding, monitors churn risk, and drives expansion—all in the tools your team already uses.

The Bigger Picture: Aligning Product, Sales, and Success

There’s also a cultural benefit to this setup. By integrating product data into HubSpot, you create a shared language between teams. Sales sees how customers actually engage with what they sold. CS sees early signals of renewal risk. Product learns which features drive expansion.

This shared understanding is hard to fake. It helps teams prioritize the right accounts, respond faster, and make decisions based on behavior—not just feelings or gut instinct.

More than that, it helps SaaS businesses deliver on what they promise. If your product is delivering value, you should be able to show it. If it’s not, you should know why. With product and CRM data working together, your team doesn’t have to wait until the QBR to figure it out.

The Road Ahead

HubSpot isn’t a perfect CS solution. But when combined with product analytics, it becomes one of the most versatile platforms you can use to build a scalable, data-driven customer success function.

The best part? It’s already where your data lives.

If you’re a B2B SaaS company looking to scale retention, reduce churn, and increase expansion, it’s time to stop treating HubSpot like a silo. It’s time to turn it into a real-time, product-aware platform for customer success.

With June, that future isn’t hypothetical—it’s up and running.

title: Embedded Product Analytics: How TrueClicks Aligns Product Usage with Customer Success Using June
html:
TrueClicks, a platform built to optimize Google Ads performance, operates in one of the most results-driven verticals in SaaS. Their clients—agencies and advertisers—depend on accurate data and measurable impact.

The product is designed to deliver just that: clear insights, automated recommendations, and powerful diagnostics to maximize ad performance. But like many B2B software companies, TrueClicks encountered a familiar challenge. While the platform itself offered immense value, communicating that value to customers in an ongoing, digestible way proved harder than expected.

Internally, the team knew the product worked. They could point to countless performance improvements, cost efficiencies, and smarter bidding decisions driven by the platform. What was missing was a way to bridge the gap between product results and customer perception. The team needed to help customers see that value for themselves—and do it continuously, not just during quarterly business reviews.

TL;DR

  • TrueClicks needed a better way to communicate product value and improve retention beyond static reports and spreadsheets.
  • By integrating June, they built internal dashboards to track engagement trends and external embedded dashboards to showcase customer-specific performance data.
  • These real-time insights allowed the customer success team to act on declining usage and empowered customers to clearly see their ROI, driving higher feature adoption and easier renewals.
  • The result was a shift from reactive reporting to a data-driven, proactive customer success strategy powered by aligned product and CRM insights.

When Static Reports Fall Short

Before the change, much of TrueClicks’ reporting was static. Results were shared in spreadsheets or presentations, often manually generated and context-limited.

While this may have worked in early-stage customer relationships, it became clear that this format couldn’t keep up with client expectations. Customers wanted ongoing proof of ROI, not just a periodic snapshot. And from a customer success standpoint, this made proactive support nearly impossible.

There was also a deeper issue at play: customer engagement was increasingly hard to gauge. Were users logging in? Which features were being used regularly? Where were clients dropping off or missing opportunities to act on the platform’s insights? Without these insights, it was difficult to have truly informed conversations about adoption, value, or renewal.

Moving Toward Real-Time, Integrated Product Insights with Embedded Product Analytics

This is where TrueClicks made a pivotal shift. The team turned to June, a product & customer analytics tool designed specifically for B2B SaaS companies. The objective was to integrate product usage data more deeply into customer success operations—making it easier to understand engagement in real time and to communicate value externally. With June, the change was immediate and tangible.

Internally, the company now had access to a live dashboard showing engagement metrics by customer. These weren’t just vanity stats—they were real signals about how different users interacted with the product. The team could see usage trends, track adoption of key features, and identify moments when customers started to disengage. This allowed the CS team to focus their energy more strategically, whether that meant reaching out to provide support or reinforcing the benefits of underused tools.

The embedded metrics weren’t limited to internal use. What made the approach so effective was TrueClicks’ decision to bring these insights directly to customers. Using June’s capability to embed usage dashboards, TrueClicks created personalized customer-facing performance pages. Each customer now had a dynamic portal where they could view product metrics relevant to their own account—things like campaign improvements, saved hours, or optimization outcomes—without needing to log into the product or interpret raw data themselves.

Turning Data into Renewals

The implications for customer success were immediate. With both internal visibility and external transparency, the team had a much clearer understanding of who was getting value and who wasn’t.

Conversations with clients shifted from generic updates to specific, data-driven narratives: what you’ve done, what you’ve gained, and what you might be missing. That depth of context changed the quality of CS interactions and enabled more proactive support.

More importantly, the presence of embedded dashboards made renewals easier to manage. Clients could see the ROI of the platform continuously, not just when prompted. The ongoing visibility into results meant that the value of TrueClicks didn’t need to be re-explained at each contract cycle—it was already visible, measurable, and understood. Customers didn’t need convincing; they needed confirmation.

Embedded Product Analytics: Why Integration with Product and CRM Data Matters

For B2B SaaS companies like TrueClicks, especially those working in a vertical with clear performance outcomes, integrating product analytics with CRM systems isn’t a nice-to-have. It’s essential. June makes this integration seamless by linking behavioral product data with account-level context. This way, usage trends are never viewed in isolation. They’re tied to revenue, to success milestones, and to specific customer relationships.

That combination makes it possible to build smarter engagement strategies, tailor onboarding and support, and—critically—predict which customers are on track to renew and which might require extra attention.

In industries like SaaS, where long-term retention defines success, this kind of visibility can be a competitive advantage.

A Blueprint for Data-Driven Customer Success

TrueClicks didn’t just gain better reporting; they built a system for scalable customer engagement. They moved away from ad hoc account management and toward a structured, data-informed process where insights drive outcomes.

For the customer success team, that meant clearer priorities and more efficient use of time. For customers, it meant a deeper connection to the platform and greater trust in its results.

In the long run, these shifts don’t just improve renewals. They strengthen the overall relationship between customer and product. They make it easier to show impact, to earn advocacy, and to build loyalty. What started as a need to communicate value more clearly turned into a full transformation of how success was measured, shared, and scaled.

June helped TrueClicks close that gap, turning guesswork into precision and dashboards into growth tools. For any B2B SaaS company aiming to level up its customer success strategy, this kind of integrated, data-rich approach isn’t just useful—it’s the future.

title: Scaling Customer Insights at Luminovo: A Case Study in CRM-Integrated Product Analytics
html:
Luminovo, an AI-driven software company focused on the electronics industry, was growing steadily and believed their customer relationships were healthy—until a major client unexpectedly churned. It wasn’t just the loss of revenue that stung, but the realization that no one saw it coming. There had been no signals, no complaints, no clear warning signs.

That event forced the team to confront a tough truth: they lacked visibility into how customers were actually engaging with the product.

Without knowing which features were used, which were ignored, and whether users were extracting value, it was impossible to see churn coming—let alone prevent it.

TL;DR

  • Luminovo faced unexpected churn that revealed a lack of visibility into real product usage across customers, prompting the need for better customer success tools.
  • By implementing June, the team gained real-time insight into feature adoption, engagement trends, and account activity—information their CRM alone couldn’t provide.
  • June’s product analytics combined with CRM data allowed Luminovo to act early, personalize outreach, and guide customers toward higher-value usage.
  • The result was a shift from reactive to proactive customer success, driving stronger retention, better relationships, and more predictable growth.

CRM Alone Wasn’t Enough

Like many B2B SaaS companies, Luminovo relied on its CRM to keep track of account-level information. But over time, it became clear that while CRMs are great for storing contact data, contract dates, and customer notes, they fall short in one crucial area: tracking actual product usage.

A CRM might tell you when a renewal is due, but it can’t tell you if users have logged in this week. It won’t show you which teams are active, whether key features are being adopted, or if engagement has started to decline. And for a subscription-based product where value is realized over time, this kind of behavioral insight is essential.

Timon, a key advocate for operational change at Luminovo, understood that a reactive approach to customer success would no longer cut it. Waiting for a customer to churn before taking action was no longer acceptable. The goal was to create a proactive system—one where churn could be predicted and prevented, where the team would have the data to act early and meaningfully. That’s when Luminovo decided to bring in June, a customer analytics platform designed specifically for B2B SaaS teams that need better insight into customer engagement.

Centralizing Product Engagement in Real-Time

One of the most impactful changes June enabled was the creation of a real-time company dashboard. Before June, data was fragmented—split across tools, spreadsheets, and internal systems. Now, Luminovo’s customer success team has a clear, centralized view of each account’s product usage. They can see which features are being used, how frequently, and by which teams.

These insights allow the team to show up to calls prepared, with real context that makes conversations more relevant and productive. Rather than vague check-ins, customer success managers can now address specific behavior patterns and help customers unlock more value.

Turning Insight Into Action

The dashboard was just the beginning. Luminovo went further by setting up June’s smart alerts and computed traits. These allow the team to track usage trends across customers—like how many seats are active, how often users log in, when they were last seen in the product, and what features they engage with the most.

Revenue data from Stripe was layered in, giving a full picture that combines both financial and behavioral signals. The team then created dynamic customer segments and received real-time alerts when engagement dipped. So if a previously active user stopped logging in, someone on the team would know right away and could reach out.

Preventing Churn with Early Signals

This shift allowed Luminovo to prevent churn by addressing issues before they spiraled. A drop in engagement no longer went unnoticed. The team could immediately respond with check-ins, tailored documentation, or even personalized training sessions to help customers get back on track.

These interactions became opportunities to deliver value and strengthen relationships, rather than emergency escalations. It was no longer about saving accounts at the last minute—it was about making sure they never got to that point.

Driving Product Adoption and Customer Value

Beyond churn prevention, the team also started seeing improvements in product adoption. With visibility into which features were underutilized, customer success managers could proactively guide users to more valuable parts of the product. That led to customers realizing more value, which in turn improved satisfaction and increased the likelihood of renewal. Instead of chasing usage retroactively, Luminovo began shaping it intentionally.

For a vertical SaaS company like Luminovo, these improvements are particularly important. Their customer base operates in a specialized and often non-technical industry. That means engagement levels can vary widely across departments, locations, or business units within the same company.

A CRM might mark the entire account as active, while in reality, only a subset of users is actually engaged. June helped bring clarity to this complexity. With its CRM integration, June linked account-level information with granular product usage data, helping the team understand who was doing what, and where support was really needed.

A Unified Source of Truth

This CRM and product data integration gave Luminovo what every SaaS team needs: a unified source of truth. It turned the CRM from a static database into a live dashboard of customer health. And with that, customer success became more than just a reactive support function—it became a strategic growth lever. The team could identify upsell opportunities, reduce risk, and have more meaningful interactions with their customers.

Since adopting June, Luminovo has fully transitioned from intuition-based outreach to data-informed customer management. Their team now knows exactly when to act and how to personalize their approach.

The guesswork has been eliminated. Conversations are grounded in facts, not assumptions. And most importantly, customers are seeing more value—and sticking around longer.

The Takeaway for Growing SaaS Teams

What Luminovo’s story illustrates is that CRM alone isn’t enough—not when customer engagement happens inside the product. By layering in product usage analytics, they unlocked a new level of customer insight. For any B2B SaaS company looking to improve retention and grow efficiently, this approach is becoming non-negotiable.

June gave Luminovo the tools to make it happen, and the outcome has been a more confident, proactive, and ultimately more successful customer success function.

title: Churn Probability: Why Your CRM Alone Can’t Prevent Churn — And What to Do About It
html:
CRMs are a foundational part of how SaaS companies manage customer relationships. They offer structure, visibility, and a single source of truth for account data. From deal history to contract renewal dates, they help teams stay organized and aligned around customer information. But when it comes to identifying—and actively preventing—churn, CRM systems can fall short.

Understanding whether a customer is at risk of churning requires more than a list of account owners or timestamps of recent emails. It requires insight into behavior. Specifically, it requires a clear picture of how that customer is engaging with your product. Without that layer, teams are often left relying on anecdotal signals or lagging indicators. And by the time a churn risk becomes obvious in your CRM, it’s often too late to change the outcome.

The Blind Spot in CRM-Driven Retention

Customer relationship management systems do a good job of capturing static information—roles, contract value, renewal timelines, support activity. They help orchestrate the operational side of account management. But they don’t offer a window into what the customer is actually doing inside your product.

That’s a limitation. Because in SaaS, engagement is the real signal of customer health.

Churn rarely begins with a conversation. It starts with disengagement: a drop in logins, a decline in team-wide activity, or a failure to adopt key features. These early signs won’t be visible in a CRM record unless someone actively reports them. And if your retention strategy is built on scheduled check-ins or quarterly reviews alone, you’re reacting after momentum has already been lost.

Why Product Usage Data Matters in Identifying Churn Probability

To get ahead of churn, customer success teams need to understand not just who their customers are, but how they’re using the product—and how that usage evolves over time.

Product usage data offers this behavioral insight. It surfaces early warning signs, such as missed onboarding milestones, reduced feature engagement, or sudden inactivity. It also helps identify strong accounts—those showing consistent usage across teams, expanding their footprint, or adopting new features quickly.

When this behavioral layer is missing, it becomes difficult to prioritize outreach, understand risk, or validate whether a customer is truly seeing value. Relying on CRM data alone creates a disconnect between what a customer tells you and what they’re actually experiencing.

Closing the Gap with Product and CRM Integration

This is where June steps in. June connects product analytics data with CRM platforms like Salesforce, HubSpot, and Attio to give teams a complete, real-time view of customer health.

By embedding product usage insights into existing workflows, June enables customer success teams to assess engagement without switching tools or relying on manual data pulls. It becomes possible to segment accounts by behavioral patterns, build dynamic health scores, and trigger timely interventions based on real signals.

For example, if a high-value customer stops using a core feature two months before renewal, June surfaces that behavior so the CSM can act early—well before that churn risk turns into a decision. Similarly, if an account steadily increases usage across departments, it becomes an obvious candidate for expansion, and the team can initiate that conversation with clear data to support the outreach.

Elevating Success Strategy in Vertical SaaS

For vertical SaaS companies, the need for this integration is often even more acute. Many of these businesses serve industries where users aren’t necessarily technical, and onboarding is more involved. Customers may rely on the product for critical workflows, but their engagement can be fragile if those workflows aren’t adopted successfully.

In this context, the ability to track how individual users or teams are progressing becomes essential. A CRM might tell you that an account is up for renewal. But June can show whether that customer has completed key onboarding steps, whether engagement is distributed across teams, and whether their usage reflects actual product value.

This level of insight allows customer success managers to tailor their approach—not just by account tier or contract size, but based on real interaction with the product. For vertical SaaS, where each customer represents significant long-term value, that level of precision can make a measurable difference in retention and growth.

Churn Probability: From Visibility to Action

Preventing churn is less about predicting a risk score and more about equipping your team with timely, relevant information that helps them act.

When you combine the relationship data in your CRM with the behavioral insights from your product, you move from a static account view to a dynamic, contextual understanding of customer health. That allows CSMs to personalize their outreach, product teams to prioritize improvements, and leadership to track retention risk with greater confidence.

June makes this operationally viable. It gives teams a way to monitor engagement continuously, surface the right accounts at the right moment, and connect retention efforts directly to usage data—not just anecdotal feedback or contract details.

Moving Beyond CRM-Only Retention Strategies

CRMs aren’t going anywhere. They’re essential to running a customer-facing organization. But they aren’t designed to show you whether a customer is on track to succeed—or to churn. For that, you need to understand behavior.

June adds this behavioral layer, bridging the gap between systems of record and systems of insight. It equips customer success teams with the tools to move from reactive support to proactive, informed retention strategy.

For SaaS businesses looking to reduce churn and strengthen long-term relationships, the message is clear: don’t just track the customer. Understand how they’re using your product. And make that insight part of your daily decisions—not just a post-mortem after the contract ends.

title: Making Retention Measurable: The KPIs Every Customer Success Team Should Monitor
html:
For B2B SaaS companies, where acquisition costs are high and payback periods are long, every customer retained is a compounding win. Tracking retention KPIs is the only way to truly understand whether you're building long-term relationships or leaking value over time.

Retention metrics are the bridge between daily operations and strategic decisions. They tell you whether your onboarding is working, if your product is delivering value, and if your success team is focusing on the right accounts. Without clear visibility into retention KPIs, it becomes almost impossible to make proactive choices or prove the ROI of customer success work.

TL;DR

  • In B2B SaaS, customer retention KPIs are essential for measuring the health and longevity of your customer relationships—and ensuring sustainable revenue growth.
  • Key metrics like customer retention rate, customer lifetime value, revenue churn, and customer health score each offer a different lens on where customers are succeeding or slipping.
  • June helps customer success teams track and act on these KPIs by combining real-time product usage data with CRM insights, enabling better segmentation, prioritization, and risk prevention.
  • With clear visibility into customer behavior and trends, teams can intervene earlier, support renewals more effectively, and surface new expansion opportunities—all grounded in data, not assumptions.

Understanding the Metrics Behind Retention

There are several KPIs that help measure retention, each highlighting a different aspect of the customer relationship.

Let's dive into the most common and important ones together, and see what role they play in each phase of customer retention.

Customer Retention Rate: Your Baseline Signal

Customer retention rate is perhaps the most straightforward KPI, but it's also one of the most telling. It simply tells you how many customers stayed over a given time period, excluding any new business. While simple, this number gives you a powerful sense of whether your product and your success efforts are working.

If you're closing deals but struggling to keep those accounts over six or twelve months, your revenue is essentially leaking.

Tracking this rate consistently gives you a view into how different customer segments behave. For example, you might find that customers in certain industries or team sizes are more likely to stay, which helps refine your ideal customer profile. June allows you to segment retention rates across any CRM or product dimension—plan type, geography, feature usage—so you can see where you’re strong and where improvements are needed.

Customer Lifetime Value: The Financial Lens on Retention

Customer lifetime value (LTV) goes beyond simple account retention—it tells you how valuable a customer is over the full span of their engagement with your business. It accounts for how much they pay, how long they stay, and how much they might expand. For customer success teams, customer lifetime value becomes a north star: it helps prioritize efforts by showing which accounts can generate the most impact over time.

LTV isn’t static. It changes based on how customers use the product and whether they adopt new features or upgrade to higher tiers. With June, you can connect product behavior with expansion signals to identify accounts with high LTV potential—those who are consistently using core features, inviting teammates, or increasing their usage footprint. That visibility helps you focus your efforts and build stronger business cases for renewals and upsells.

Revenue Churn Rate: Measuring What You’re Losing

While LTV shows potential, revenue churn rate shows loss. It tells you how much recurring revenue you’re losing from existing customers—through cancellations, downgrades, or contract reductions. This metric is particularly important in SaaS because churned revenue is revenue you have to replace just to stay flat. Even modest churn can quietly erode what looks like top-line growth.

Monitoring revenue churn at the account and segment level is crucial. A few large downgrades can be more damaging than a dozen small churns. With June’s CRM and product data integration, you can trace churn patterns back to product usage—or lack thereof. Were key features abandoned weeks before cancellation? Was usage flatlining during the renewal cycle? By connecting these dots, you gain the insight to act earlier next time.

Customer Health Score: The Early Warning System

The customer health score is where retention becomes predictive. It’s a composite metric that blends different signals—product engagement, support activity, CRM milestones, even NPS responses—to give you a real-time picture of how likely a customer is to stay, churn, or grow. Customer health scores are never perfect, but when designed well, they offer your team a reliable compass.

The challenge, of course, is building a health score that actually reflects reality. That’s where June shines. By pulling in both product analytics and CRM attributes, June helps you build contextual, dynamic health scores based on what actually matters in your customer journey. You can customize your score based on activation steps completed, feature usage frequency, account stage, and more. When the score drops, your team knows exactly what to check and how to respond.

Making KPIs Actionable with June

Measuring these KPIs is one thing—making them actionable is another. That’s where June comes in. At its core, June connects product analytics and CRM data, making it easier for customer success teams to track, interpret, and act on retention KPIs at scale.

June helps you understand what customers are doing in your product, not just what they bought or what stage of the funnel they’re in. By syncing product usage data with HubSpot, Salesforce, or Attio, June creates a complete view of each customer and allows you to filter, segment, and monitor cohorts over time. You can see which accounts are drifting and which are growing. More importantly, you can understand why.

For customer success, this is game-changing. Instead of operating based on intuition or account notes, you work with actual product behavior. You know which features are being used, how often, and by whom. You can build dashboards that track engagement across specific milestones—onboarding steps, feature adoption, team activation—and compare how high-value customers differ from those at risk.

Embedded dashboards make this insight even more powerful. With June, you can share live product usage data with your customers directly. This helps them understand their own value from your tool, increases transparency, and aligns everyone around shared goals. A customer who knows where they stand is far more likely to renew, expand, and advocate.

Preventing Churn, Enabling Renewals and Growth

Tracking retention KPIs isn’t just about reporting—it’s about prevention. When you monitor usage and health indicators closely, you spot the subtle signs that precede churn: reduced login frequency, fewer active seats, stalled onboarding. June lets you build views to surface these trends early so that your team can intervene before it’s too late.

Renewals become more predictable too. With product and CRM data in sync, you can run account reviews based on facts, not guesswork. You can show stakeholders how adoption has evolved and how engagement links to outcomes. That clarity builds trust—and trust closes renewals.

On the growth side, retention KPIs help surface expansion opportunities. Customers who consistently adopt new features or who have maxed out their plan often signal readiness for upsell. With June, you can spot these behaviors automatically and route them to the right CSM or AE, increasing expansion revenue without increasing headcount.

Retention as a Strategy, Not a Metric

Ultimately, retention KPIs are not just numbers to track—they’re indicators of your product-market fit, your onboarding quality, your support effectiveness, and your long-term value. In B2B SaaS, customer retention is not owned by one department. It’s a shared outcome that depends on the collaboration between product, customer success, sales, and marketing.

June equips customer-facing teams to take control of that outcome. By integrating usage data into your daily workflows, June helps you understand what drives retention—and what doesn’t. With clear, contextualized insights, you can align your customer success model to what’s really happening in your product and keep improving from there.

When retention becomes part of your operating system, not just a KPI to report on, your business becomes more stable, your customers more loyal, and your team more strategic. That’s what June is built to support.

title: How to Align Your Customer Success Models With Real Customer Behavior
html:
When you think about building a strong customer success function, it’s tempting to imagine there’s a one-size-fits-all blueprint. But the truth is, there isn’t. A customer success model is not just a set of processes or playbooks you plug into your business. It’s a strategic choice about how you engage, support, and grow your customers based on who they are, how they behave, and what your product actually demands from them to succeed.

In B2B SaaS, a customer success model defines the structure and intensity of your customer relationships. It’s not about forcing every account into a series of automated emails, nor about assigning a dedicated manager to every single user. It’s about matching your resources and actions to the needs of your customers, in a way that makes sense for your product, your business goals, and the stage you’re in.

Choosing the wrong model—or applying the right model to the wrong accounts—doesn’t just hurt efficiency. It leaves customers without the support they need, creates friction, and ultimately hurts retention and growth. That’s why it’s so important to understand the different types of customer success models and how to apply them intentionally.

TL;DR

  • A customer success model defines how a SaaS company engages and supports its customers, ranging from high-touch personal relationships to fully automated tech-touch systems.
  • Choosing the right model is critical, especially for vertical SaaS businesses, where balancing deep support and scalability can directly impact retention and growth.
  • June helps customer success teams make data-driven decisions by combining product usage and CRM data, making it easier to assign the right engagement model based on how customers behave—not just what contract they signed.
  • By using real-time behavioral insights, companies can proactively support onboarding, identify expansion opportunities, and mitigate churn risk, dynamically adjusting their customer success approach as customer needs evolve.

The Main Customer Success Models in B2B SaaS

Broadly speaking, there are four primary customer success models that SaaS businesses tend to use: high-touch, low-touch, hybrid, and tech-touch. Each comes with different expectations for how much human interaction a customer receives and what kind of resources you allocate.

In a high-touch model, customer success managers work closely with a small portfolio of customers, often providing regular check-ins, strategic guidance, and personalized support. This approach works well for complex products, enterprise clients, and high-value accounts where deep relationships are key to renewal and expansion.

The low-touch model leans more on scalable communication. CSMs manage larger portfolios, combining automated engagement with targeted human interactions based on key triggers. It fits well when customers are somewhat self-sufficient but still benefit from occasional check-ins.

Hybrid models blend these approaches. Some accounts receive white-glove support while others follow more structured, lightly personalized programs, depending on contract value, complexity, or strategic importance.

Tech-touch models take scalability even further. Engagement happens primarily through product-led onboarding, in-app messaging, help centers, and automated workflows, with little to no assigned CSM involvement. It works best when the product is intuitive, self-service is strong, and account value doesn’t justify much manual support.

Why Choosing the Right Model Matters Even More in Vertical SaaS

Vertical SaaS companies face particular challenges when it comes to choosing a customer success model. Serving a specialized industry means customers often expect expert-level guidance, not just technical support. They rely on your platform to deliver outcomes that are deeply integrated into their daily workflows, not just nice-to-have efficiencies.

Because vertical markets tend to be smaller, retention becomes absolutely critical. Losing a customer isn't just a revenue hit—it can hurt reputation within a tight community. On the other hand, resources are always finite, and providing high-touch service to every single account isn't sustainable.

That’s why vertical SaaS companies must be strategic. They need to identify where high-touch service will drive long-term expansion, and where a lighter model can still deliver success without overextending the team. Behavioral data and usage insights become key to making these decisions with precision, not guesswork.

How June Helps Customer Success Teams Choose Smarter Models

This is where June fits perfectly into the picture. June connects your product usage data with your CRM, giving you a unified view of how customers are actually interacting with your platform, not just what their contract says or how many users they’ve provisioned.

Through June, customer success teams can track engagement milestones, feature adoption rates, activity patterns, and overall customer health scores. By analyzing this behavior, it becomes clear which clients are thriving, which are struggling, and which are simply coasting without achieving real value.

This visibility allows teams to match the right customer success model to the right segment. Accounts showing strong engagement can be moved toward a tech-touch or low-touch cadence, while customers falling behind on key onboarding milestones might be escalated to high-touch support.

June doesn’t just show you the data. It helps you act on it, making your customer success model dynamic—adapting to the customer’s behavior, not a rigid internal structure.

Improving Onboarding Success Rates with Behavior-Based Models

Onboarding is one of the clearest moments where having flexible customer success models pays off. When new accounts sign up, they don't all progress at the same pace. Some will move quickly through setup and early activation, while others will get stuck and risk disengagement within the first few weeks.

Using June, it becomes easy to identify which customers are lagging behind. If a user hasn’t completed key steps or activated core features within a certain time frame, it signals the need for a more personalized, high-touch intervention. Rather than waiting for a quarterly review or for the customer to complain, you can immediately adapt your approach—offering a guided session, a check-in call, or tailored resources to help them get back on track.

By shifting resources based on real-time behavior, you ensure that more customers achieve early success, reducing churn risk significantly. At the same time, customers who are naturally self-sufficient can continue through automated onboarding processes without overwhelming your team.

Scaling Expansion Opportunities with Smart Segmentation

Expansion is another area where behavioral segmentation transforms customer success. Not every active customer is ready for an upsell or cross-sell. Pushing expansion too early—or at the wrong time—can damage trust and hurt relationships.

With June, you can spot when the right conditions are emerging. Maybe a team has started using new features at a higher rate, or maybe user seats have expanded across new departments. These are signs that the customer is deriving value and growing internally, even if they haven’t explicitly raised their hand.

By identifying these accounts early, you can shift from a tech-touch to a more personalized low-touch or high-touch engagement, offering strategic conversations about how to formalize their broader usage. It turns expansion from a sales play into a success-led conversation, driven by real data instead of guesses.

Proactively Managing Churn Risks Before They Escalate

Churn rarely happens overnight. The signals appear weeks or even months before a cancellation email ever lands. Customers start using fewer features. Team logins decrease. Core workflows get abandoned.

With June’s ability to monitor engagement trends in real time, customer success teams can surface these churn risk signals early. When a customer’s activity drops, rather than waiting for a renewal to go south, you can intervene proactively—switching the account to a high-touch recovery sequence, re-engaging stakeholders, and working to rebuild value.

Again, the model adapts to the behavior. Low-touch accounts can move into a higher support tier when needed, and once they stabilize, they can return to a lighter engagement cadence. It’s a dynamic system that lets you manage risk much more effectively without exhausting your team’s bandwidth.

Building a Customer Success Function That Evolves With Your Business

The biggest mistake companies make with customer success models is assuming they’re static. They’re not. They need to evolve as your customer base grows, your product matures, and your business priorities shift.

By connecting product data and CRM insights through June, customer success teams can stop flying blind. You can design a flexible, intelligent engagement model that responds to customer needs in real time, helping you drive better onboarding, stronger expansion, and healthier renewals—without burning out your team or leaving opportunities on the table.

Choosing the right model isn’t about picking one customer success framework forever. It’s about having the visibility and agility to adapt as your customers evolve. With the right tools, like June, you can build a system that doesn’t just serve your customers better—it grows with them.

Timon, one of the company’s biggest advocates for improving customer success, knew they needed a change. He pushed his team to adopt a tool that would help them stay ahead of churn, better understand customer behaviour, and make sure users were getting the most out of Luminovo. The goal wasn’t just to react to churn—but to prevent it from happening in the first place.

The Solution

1. A real-time company dashboard for customer success

Luminovo’s customer success team now uses June’s company dashboard to get a clear, instant view of every customer’s engagement. Before, they had to piece together fragmented data from different sources, making it hard to get a full picture. Now, everything is in one place, which helps them:

  • Track which features each customer is actually using (and which ones they’re ignoring).
  • Understand adoption trends and identify customers who might need extra help.
  • Give Customer Success Managers full context before they jump on a call or write an email—no more guessing!

Having all this data at their fingertips means that when a CSM reaches out to a customer, the conversation is much more tailored. Instead of generic check-ins, they can ask specific questions like, “Hey, we noticed you haven’t used [Feature X] in a while. Is there anything we can do to help?” . This approach not only helps customers get more value from the product but also builds stronger relationships.

2. Smart alerts & saved audiences to stay ahead of churn

Instead of waiting for churn to happen, the team set up automated tracking using computed traits like active seats, usage trends, last seen activity, and revenue data from Stripe. With this, they:

  • Create saved audiences to group customers by engagement levels, so they know who’s thriving and who’s at risk.
  • Get notified instantly in Slack when a customer shows signs of disengagement, allowing them to step in before it’s too late.

The alert system has been a game-changer. Previously, a customer could slowly stop engaging with the product without anyone noticing. Now, if someone who was active suddenly drops off, the team is instantly aware and can take action—whether that means offering a check-in call, sending relevant documentation, or even running a mini-training session to help them get back on track.

The Outcome: Proactive, Data-Driven Customer Success

Since rolling out June, Luminovo’s approach to customer success has completely changed for the better:

  • Fewer surprises, more control: Instead of getting blindsided by churn, the team can now see early warning signs and take action before it happens.
  • Smarter customer interactions: CSMs now have all the insights they need before talking to a customer, making their calls and emails way more relevant and impactful.
  • Better feature adoption: by identifying which features are underused, the team can guide customers toward valuable functionality they might be missing out on.
  • Higher retention rates: more engaged customers mean fewer churned accounts, leading to stronger long-term relationships and more predictable revenue.

With June, Luminovo has shifted from being reactive to proactive. Now, they don’t just track customer engagement—they actually drive it. The combination of real-time insights, smart alerts, and data-driven outreach has empowered their team to take a hands-on approach to customer success. Instead of scrambling to save customers at the last minute, they’re building habits that keep users engaged from day one.

For any growing SaaS company, keeping customers happy and engaged is just as important as acquiring new ones. Thanks to June, Luminovo can ensure that their users aren’t just signing up—they’re sticking around, growing with the product, and ultimately becoming long-term advocates.

TrueClicks, a PPC optimization platform, helps agencies and advertisers maximize the performance of their Google Ads accounts. While their platform provides deep insights and automated recommendations, they faced a common challenge: proving the ROI of their product to customers in a way that was both clear and compelling.

Wijnand, the founder of TrueClicks, wanted an effective way to showcase key performance metrics to customers, demonstrating the tangible impact of the platform’s optimizations. The goal was to improve adoption, drive engagement, and make it easier for customer success teams to highlight value. However, traditional reporting methods—such as static reports or spreadsheets—lacked the interactive and dynamic elements needed to truly drive customer engagement.

The Solution

To address this, TrueClicks integrated June, a product analytics tool designed for B2B companies, with a strong focus on customer success use cases. The solution included two key elements:

  1. Internal Usage Dashboard TrueClicks implemented an internal analytics dashboard to track product engagement and usage trends in real time. This dashboard allowed Wijnand and his cs and sales team to monitor key metrics such as:
    • Active Users: Weekly and monthly active users, identifying usage patterns and engagement drops.
    • Feature Adoption: Tracking which features were being used and by whom, helping inform customer success strategies.
    • Top Events: Logging user interactions such as viewed reports, executed queries, and edited audiences, ensuring a clear understanding of user behavior.
    • Usage Trends: Detecting increases or declines in engagement to proactively intervene when necessary.
      This internal tracking helped the team focus on the right customers, prioritize outreach, and improve overall retention.

    • Simplify renewal conversations by giving customers easy access to ROI-driven insights.

The Outcome: increased adoption and higher perceived value

The implementation of internal analytics and embedded customer-facing metrics led to significant improvements in customer engagement and retention for TrueClicks:

title: Making Product Usage Count: How Behavioral Segmentation Boosts SaaS Retention and Expansion
html:
In B2B SaaS, not all customers are the same. Even when they come from the same industry, have similar company sizes, or pay for the same plan, their actual behavior inside your product can look completely different. Some teams log in every day and fully adopt your core workflows. Others barely get past onboarding or use only a fraction of your features. That’s where behavioral segmentation becomes essential.

Behavioral segmentation means grouping your customers based on what they actually do—how often they use your product, which features they engage with, how long they stay active, and how their habits evolve over time. It’s about looking at usage patterns rather than company traits, and making decisions based on observed behavior rather than assumptions.

This approach is especially valuable in SaaS, where your business model depends not just on signups, but on continued engagement, retention, and expansion. Understanding behavior at scale—and segmenting your customer base accordingly—lets you act more precisely, prioritize the right accounts, and improve outcomes across the board.

What we'll cover today:

  • Behavioral segmentation helps you understand how different groups of customers actually use your SaaS product, rather than relying on static traits like industry or company size. By analyzing real user behavior—such as feature adoption, frequency of use, or time to onboard—you can create more meaningful customer segments that reflect engagement and value realization.
  • When you identify which behaviors correlate with retention, expansion, and higher LTV, you can build strategies that guide more customers in that direction. For example, accounts that engage early with a core feature or reach a key milestone within 30 days often become long-term customers. Behavioral segmentation lets you map these patterns and use them to inform onboarding, in-app messaging, and success interventions.
  • June helps you run behavioral segmentation at scale by combining product usage data with CRM context, giving your team a unified view of how different types of accounts interact with the product. You can analyze behavior by company type, team size, lifecycle stage, or any CRM attribute—then compare usage patterns to find what makes your best customers stick and grow.
  • Customer success teams can use these insights to prioritize accounts, personalize outreach, and act earlier—before risk turns into churn or opportunity is missed. Whether it’s spotting a disengaged team, guiding a new user cohort toward success, or identifying expansion-ready segments, behavioral segmentation powered by June helps CS teams go from reactive to strategic.

Why Segmenting by Behavior Unlocks More Than Retention

In practice, behavioral segmentation is often associated with churn prevention. And that makes sense—looking for patterns like usage drops, missed milestones, or feature neglect is a smart way to spot risk before it’s too late. But the real potential goes much further.

By understanding how different segments of users interact with your product, you can start to identify the behaviors that correlate with success. You begin to see which actions lead to higher lifetime value, which features drive stickiness, and which patterns signal a readiness to upgrade or expand. And once those patterns are visible, you can build playbooks around them.

Maybe it’s that teams who use one particular automation feature in their first 30 days tend to renew at higher rates. Or perhaps power users of a certain report become advocates who drive internal expansion. These aren’t assumptions—you can find these signals in the data. But only if you’re looking at behavior, not just demographics or deal size.

Behavioral segmentation becomes the foundation for smarter onboarding, more personalized customer success strategies, better product decisions, and ultimately, stronger revenue growth.

Identifying What Drives Value (and Who’s Experiencing It)

One of the biggest challenges in SaaS is identifying the difference between an account that looks good on paper and one that’s actually healthy. A CRM tech stack might tell you the contract value, renewal date, or who the buyer was. But it won’t tell you whether that account has truly realized value from your product—or whether it’s coasting on inertia and one champion who’s barely holding things together.

This is where behavioral segmentation becomes a strategic advantage. When you start grouping users by what they’ve done, not just who they are, you can see where your product is actually delivering value. You can find the clusters of accounts that use key features often, reach core milestones quickly, or expand usage organically over time. These are your real success stories. And once you understand the common behaviors within these segments, you can reverse-engineer them into your broader strategy.

Instead of guessing what makes a customer successful, you start with proof. That clarity can influence everything—from which features to highlight in onboarding, to how your CS team structures outreach, to which customers are most likely to buy more seats or upgrade plans.

How June Helps Map Behavior to Strategy

This is exactly where June comes in. With June, you can go beyond top-level metrics and start analyzing how groups of customers behave across your product. You’re not just looking at individual events—you’re mapping patterns, identifying key moments, and linking them to real business outcomes.

June connects product usage data with CRM context, so you can slice and segment customers based on both behavior and business data. You might look at how fast onboarding happens for customers in a certain industry, or how expansion correlates with early feature adoption across teams. You might compare high LTV accounts to average ones and spot the behaviors that consistently show up among your most valuable users.

By segmenting customers this way, your team can stop treating accounts as a monolith. You can personalize your B2B SaaS growth strategy based on usage trends, guide users toward the behaviors that lead to success, and spot emerging risks or opportunities before they show up in a renewal conversation.

And because June makes this data accessible to customer success—not just product or data teams—it becomes something you can use in real time, not just in quarterly reporting. Your CS team knows which customers are drifting, which are ready for a deeper conversation, and which need a simple nudge to unlock more value.

Use Cases Where Behavioral Segmentation Changes the Game

There’s a clear advantage in retention. When customers stop using core features or fall behind on onboarding, they rarely announce it. They just quietly disengage. With behavioral segmentation, you can track these patterns across your base and build alert systems or churn prediction models and workflows that bring those accounts back before they leave.

It’s just as powerful when you’re trying to drive expansion. If you know that teams who hit certain usage milestones tend to expand within 90 days, you can track which accounts are on that path. You can design touchpoints, in-app nudges, or success playbooks that align with their stage and behavior. The result isn’t just more upgrades—it’s more organic, better-timed conversations that customers are more likely to respond to.

And then there’s the impact on product development. When you can group accounts by success outcomes and tie that back to specific features or habits, your product team has a clearer roadmap. You’re no longer building for hypotheticals—you’re doubling down on what actually drives impact.

A Customer Success Team That Works Smarter, Not Harder

From a CS perspective, behavioral segmentation is what helps you stop reacting and start leading. You no longer need to treat every account the same or wait for issues to escalate. You can focus your attention on the segments that matter most—those at risk, those with momentum, and those that are falling somewhere in between.

June gives customer success teams the visibility they need to act early and act with confidence. Whether it’s sending tailored success emails based on usage milestones, adjusting check-in cadences based on engagement trends, or building renewal strategies rooted in real product adoption—these are the kinds of moves that make success feel less like support and more like strategy.

Closing the Gap Between Behavior and Business Growth

Behavioral segmentation isn’t just another analytics feature—it’s a shift in how you understand your customers. It allows you to stop guessing who your best users are, stop treating all accounts equally, and start designing your strategy around what people are actually doing in your product.

That shift leads to better onboarding. It leads to more meaningful engagement. And ultimately, it leads to higher retention, stronger expansion revenue, and a clearer view of what success really looks like in your SaaS business.

With June, that shift becomes simple to execute. It gives your product and customer teams a shared view of behavior across segments—so everyone is working from the same playbook, guided by the same signals, and aligned around the same goal: helping your customers realize more value, more often.
